If you're looking for something even more unusual and experimental, you might enjoy the following albums:

* Coil - The Ape of Naples (2005) - This album is a posthumous release of previously unheard material by the influential industrial band Coil. It features a unique blend of dark ambiance, noise, and melodic elements.
* Grouper - Ruins (2014) - This album is a deeply personal and introspective work that explores the use of space and silence in music. It features hauntingly beautiful vocal melodies and sparse, atmospheric instrumentation.
* Holly Herndon - Proto (2019) - This album is a groundbreaking work that explores the intersection of electronic music and artificial intelligence. It features collaborations with AI entities and experiments with vocal manipulation and processing.
* Keiji Haino - Watashi Dake? (1981) - This album is a challenging and avant-garde work by the Japanese musician Keiji Haino. It features extended improvisations on guitar, vocals, and percussion, and it is not for the faint of heart.
* Nurse with Wound - Soliloquy for Lilith (1988) - This album is a pioneering work of industrial music that explores the use of noise and dissonance. It features a wide range of unconventional sounds and textures, and it is not for the faint of heart.
* The Residents - Eskimo (1979) - This album is a surreal and bizarre work by the enigmatic band The Residents. It features a unique blend of folk, tribal, and electronic elements, and it is a true cult classic.

If you enjoy drone music, you might enjoy the following albums:

* Tim Hecker - Harmony in Ultraviolet (2006) - This album is a masterful work of ambient drone music that explores the use of texture and atmosphere. It features layered, evolving soundscapes that are both beautiful and unsettling.
* Félicia Atkinson - The Flower and the Vessel (2019) - This album is a stunning work of experimental drone music that incorporates elements of field recordings and spoken word. It is a deeply personal and introspective work that explores the relationship between sound and memory.
* Grouper - Ruins (2014) - This album is a hauntingly beautiful work of drone music that explores the use of space and silence. It features sparse, atmospheric instrumentation and haunting vocal melodies that will transport you to another world.
* Ellen Arkbro - For Organ and Brass (2018) - This album is a minimalist work of drone music that explores the intersection of electronic and acoustic instrumentation. It features a unique blend of organ and brass that creates a deeply meditative and immersive listening experience.
* Sunn O))) - Life Metal (2019) - This album is a heavy and powerful work of drone metal that explores the use of distortion and volume. It is not for the faint of heart, but it will certainly satisfy fans of the genre.

If you're looking for something darker, you might enjoy the following albums:

* Sunn O))) - Life Metal (2019) - This album is a heavy and powerful work of drone metal that explores the use of distortion and volume. It is not for the faint of heart, but it will certainly satisfy fans of the genre.
* Deathspell Omega - Fas - Ite, Maledicti, in Ignem Aeternum (2008) - This album is a classic of the black metal genre that explores themes of blasphemy and despair. It features intense, chaotic instrumentation and powerful, guttural vocals.
* The Haxan Cloak - Excavation (2013) - This album is a dark and atmospheric work of experimental music that explores the use of noise and distortion. It is not for the faint of heart, but it will certainly challenge and reward the listener.
* Zola Jesus - Okovi (2017) - This album is a haunting and emotive work of gothic-influenced pop music. It features powerful, operatic vocals and dense, atmospheric instrumentation that will transport you to a darker world.
* The Body - I Have Fought Against It, But I Can't Any Longer (2018) - This album is a punishing work of industrial-influenced metal that explores themes of despair and hopelessness. It features crushing, distorted instrumentation and harrowing vocal performances.

If you're looking for music that incorporates vocoder vocals, you might enjoy the following albums:

* Daft Punk - Discovery (2001) - This album is a classic of the French house genre that heavily incorporates vocoder vocals. It features catchy, danceable beats and futuristic, robotic vocals that will transport you to a different world.
* The Postal Service - Give Up (2003) - This album is a classic of indie pop that incorporates vocoder vocals in a subtle and effective way. It features catchy, melodic songs and dreamy, electronic production that will appeal to fans of the genre.
* Gorillaz - Plastic Beach (2010) - This album is a unique blend of hip hop, pop, and electronic music that incorporates vocoder vocals in a playful and innovative way. It features a wide range of guest artists and a varied, colorful sound that will appeal to fans of the genre.
* Janelle Monáe - The ArchAndroid (2010) - This album is a concept album that incorporates vocoder vocals in a highly stylized and theatrical way. It features a unique blend of R&B, funk, and soul that is both futuristic and retro.
* YACHT - See Mystery Lights (2009) - This album is a playful and experimental work of synthpop that incorporates vocoder vocals in a variety of ways. It features catchy, danceable beats and a wide range of vocal styles that will appeal to fans of the genre.
